claim: The dciodvfy person-name check is purely syntactic and carries no information about whether a value names a person, an organisation or a tool, so no third-party validator in the panel can adjudicate the sentinel classification.
value: probed on eight values: TotalSegmentator, SIEMENS, MyName and 12345 are all flagged; ACME Corp^, ^TotalSegmentator, Total^Segmentator and Doe^Jane^^Dr^PhD are all clean. The flag separates strings containing a caret from strings that do not.
floor: not applicable, this row describes a validator behaviour rather than quoting a rate
dropped: nothing; all eight probe values are reported
validator_version: dicom3tools 1.00~20240118131615, the registered build, not the 20260701065818 build this study ran
command: reported in COLOPHON_ADDENDUM_03.md section 1; not re-run here
status_note: A retraction, recorded as one. An earlier instruction was to cross the sentinel classification against this flag as an external validity check. The probe shows the check is syntactic, so the cross-check was never built and the table goes into Methods as a mechanistic account of why a validator cannot answer this question, never as corroboration that one does.
notes: The probe was run against the registered dicom3tools build rather than the build this study ran. The behaviour is a property of the VR check and not of the message classes counted in Results, so the DEV-01 exposure analysis does not bear on it.
